sections.heading: C — Driver education, permits, fees
sections.markdown:
## C — Driver Education, Permits, Fees (Handbook Section 3)
Pedagogic emphasis: permit supervision and holding-period rules carry the most test leverage here [A01].

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Utah high-school classroom driver education requires twenty-seven hours of classroom teaching [A01].
Why it matters: separates the high-school path from commercial and online hour totals.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
A commercial or private-school classroom course requires eighteen hours of instruction [A01].
Why it matters: candidates often swap this total with the high-school total.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
An approved online or home-study course requires thirty hours of study [A01].
Why it matters: this is the largest of the three classroom-hour options.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Every path adds six hours of behind-the-wheel instruction plus six hours of observation with a licensed instructor [A01].
Why it matters: the two six-hour blocks apply regardless of classroom path.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Out-of-state certificates must meet Utah hour totals and include a completed DLD200 form [A01].
Why it matters: missing hours can be made up at an approved Utah driving school.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Out-of-state online or home-study certificates are not accepted in Utah [A01].
Why it matters: online students must retrain through an approved Utah course.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
Applicants aged fifteen through eighteen must finish driver education and log forty hours with a parent or guardian, including ten after sunset [A01].
Why it matters: the supervised-hours rule is a frequent exam trap.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
Adults nineteen or older without a license may qualify after holding a learner permit for ninety days with forty hours of driving including ten after sunset, or by finishing driver education to waive the wait [A02].
Why it matters: older beginners choose between waiting with practice or schooling.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
A driver younger than eighteen may drive a Class D vehicle only with an approved instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, a signing adult, or another licensed adult aged twenty-one or older with parental permission [A02].
Why it matters: the supervisor must sit in the front seat next to the applicant.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
An entry-level learner permit requires an appointment with documents and fee, a passed knowledge test and eye test, a minimum age of fifteen, and it stays valid for eighteen months while the permit stays on hand [A02].
Why it matters: entry scores last eighteen months and renewal triggers a retest.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A03
A six-month renewal permit needs a minimum age of sixteen, driver education completion, six months of holding for teens and ninety days for adults, possession on hand, and scores valid for twelve months [A03].
Why it matters: holding time and score life change with age and permit type.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A03
A sixteen-year-old license holder faces a nighttime limit from midnight to five in the morning plus a family-only passenger limit for six months, with work, school, farm and emergency exceptions [A03].
Why it matters: sixteen is the only age with added night and rider limits.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A04
Listed fees include nineteen for a learner permit, thirty-nine for a provisional license, fifty-two for a regular license and renewal, twenty-three for a duplicate, and eight for a driving record [A04].
Why it matters: fee numbers are exact and easily confused on the test.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0019]

High-yield focus: classroom totals, supervised-driving totals, permit validity, holding periods, supervisor rules, youthful limits and listed fees [A04].
Misconceptions: eighteen hours is commercial not high school; online out-of-state is rejected; eighteen has no hold but needs schooling [A01].
Mnemonic: twenty-seven high, eighteen trade, thirty screen.
Glossary: learner permit is supervised driving permission; DLD200 is the out-of-state training form; provisional license is the underage license.
